content.value_statement: Rust projects can become hard to maintain when crates, dependencies, tests, and CI grow without clear boundaries. This skill gives practical patterns for workspace design, dependency hygiene, testing, tracing, and quality gates.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use a Cargo workspace and how to structure crates.
Defines crate boundary patterns for core, adapters, app, and binary layers.
Recommends dependency hygiene practices, including workspace dependencies, features, and audit tooling.
Outlines unit, integration, end-to-end, property, fuzz, and doctest strategies.
Provides tracing, logging, Clippy, formatting, testing, and CI quality guidance.
limitations: Does not inspect a repository unless the user provides project files or asks for code review.
Does not replace Rust compiler, Clippy, cargo-audit, or cargo-deny results.
May need adaptation for embedded, kernel, or highly regulated Rust environments.
Focuses on project practices, not low-level unsafe Rust verification.

use_cases.title: Plan a new service workspace
use_cases.description: Define crates, boundaries, dependency policy, and initial CI for a Rust service before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review an existing Rust repository
use_cases.description: Identify architecture drift, dependency sprawl, testing gaps, and logging issues in a growing Rust codebase.

use_cases.title: Standardize team Rust practices
use_cases.description: Create shared guidance for module layout, public APIs, error handling, tests, and quality gates.

prompt_templates.title: Create a workspace plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new Rust project.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am starting a Rust project with a CLI and library. Propose a Cargo workspace layout, crate responsibilities, and first quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review crate boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing workspace layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust workspace structure for boundary problems. Point out misplaced dependencies, public API risks, and simpler crate splits.

prompt_templates.title: Design testing gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing and CI planning for a service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a testing and CI strategy for this Rust service. Include unit, integration, end-to-end, Clippy, formatting, audit, and coverage guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for production scale
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced staged cleanup for a mature Rust repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this mature Rust repository, propose a staged architecture cleanup. Preserve behavior while improving dependencies, features, tracing, tests, and release confidence.

output_examples.input: I have a Rust API crate that imports SQLx from core domain code.
output: Identifies the SQLx dependency as a boundary leak from adapter code into core logic.
Suggests moving database access behind traits and keeping domain validation synchronous when possible.
Recommends adding integration tests at the public API boundary.

output_examples.input: I need minimum CI checks for a new Rust workspace.
output: Lists formatting, Clippy, workspace tests, dependency advisory checks, and MSRV checks.
Separates mandatory gates from optional coverage and fuzzing steps.
Explains when to expand quality gates as the project grows.

best_practices: Keep core crates free from I/O, runtime, database, and HTTP dependencies.
Centralize dependency versions while keeping architecture decisions inside individual crates.
Use tests and CI gates to enforce boundaries before code reaches production.
anti_patterns: Creating many crates before there is a real boundary or release need.
Leaking application error types or anyhow errors across library APIs.
Using print debugging as production logging instead of structured tracing.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains guidance and command examples, but it does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is this useful for small Rust projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends starting simple and adding crates only when boundaries become real.

faq.question: Does it cover dependency security?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends fewer dependencies, workspace version control, cargo-audit, and cargo-deny.

faq.question: Does it replace a Rust code review?
faq.answer: No. It provides review criteria, but repository-specific risks still need project context.

faq.question: What project types does it support?
faq.answer: It covers CLI tools, services, crypto or ZK layouts, and WASM-friendly workspace patterns.
